**Solution 1 is the most likely correct answer, though its reasoning has gaps.**

**Solution 3 (answer n) is wrong.** For the code C = {000, 111}, the polarized ideal is ⟨x_i y_j : i ≠ j⟩. The Stanley–Reisner complex has facets {x_1,x_2,x_3}, {y_1,y_2,y_3}, and {x_i, y_i}. Mayer–Vietoris gives H̃_1(Δ) ≅ k², so by Hochster's formula the quotient S/P has pd ≥ 4 > 3. Its single-codeword computation also treats the pd of the quotient as the pd of the ideal, which is inconsistent.

**Solution 2 (answer 2n−1) is wrong in its reasoning.** The empty code has J_∅ equal to the unit ideal, not the maximal ideal. Its claimed generators x_i and 1−x_i are not minimal pseudo-monomials vanishing on ∅. The number 2n−1 does arise for the quotient pd if the pairs x_i y_i are included as generators, but the argument given does not establish it.

**Solution 1 (answer 2n−2) gets the right number under the standard convention.** The complete code {0^n, 1^n} gives a polarized ideal whose quotient has pd 2n−2 when the pairs {x_i, y_i} are faces, as Solution 1 assumes. Taking pd of the ideal, which is the literal reading of "pd(P(J_C))", gives 2n−3 under that setup. The value 2n−2 is recovered for the ideal when the pair generators x_i y_i are included (then the complete code gives quotient pd 2n−1). Solution 1's upper-bound argument is also shaky, since it asserts that vertices are always faces. I could not check the source paper, so the convention is the main uncertainty.

CHOICE: 1
